questions.question: Describe the contribution of Buddhism to Shramanic thought.
questions.solution_html:
• Buddhism enriched Shramanic thought- rejected Vedic ritualism and questioned
  • Brahmanical authority-emphasised the Four Noble Truths- the Eightfold Path- non-violence
  • compassion, and ethical conduct-its teachings challenged social inequalities and presented
  • liberation as achievable through wisdom, discipline, and personal effort rather than ritual
  • sacrifices.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Examine the relevance of Mukti Mission and identify the range of vocational training offered at the Mukti Mission.
questions.solution_html:
• Founded by Pandita Ramabai in 1889 at Kedgaon, Maharashtra-Mukti Mission promoted
  • women’s education, rehabilitation and empowerment-supported vulnerable women, widows
  • and children-its vocational activities have included tailoring, weaving, agriculture, printing
  • and other practical skills- encouraged economic independence, self-reliance, and dignity
  • among disadvantaged communities.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Analyse Iqbal’s concept of Khudi and its significance for the formation of an ideal Islamic personality.
questions.solution_html:
• Muhammad Iqbal’s concept of Khudi- in Urdu Khudi- translates literally to "selfhood"
  • "self-consciousness"- signifies the development of a strong, self-aware, morally responsible
  • individual- Khudi is not arrogance or mere pride- emphasises self-realisation, discipline
  • courage, creativity and purposeful action- the ideal Islamic personality cultivates spiritual
  • strength through faith and ethical responsibility- actively transforming society while striving
  • towards closeness to God.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain Ambedkar’s argument that the caste system is a "division of labourers" / rather than simply a benign "division of labour."
questions.solution_html:
• Ambedkar described caste as a “division of labourers” rather than merely a division of
  • labour- because it hierarchically organises people by birth- caste system imposes hereditary
  • occupations- restricts occupational mobility- perpetuates graded inequality- unlike functional
  • specialisation, caste denies individual freedom, dignity, fraternity and equal opportunities.
questions.final_answer: specialisation, caste denies individual freedom, dignity, fraternity and equal opportunities
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Identify the major features of Dalit-Bahujan political thought.
questions.solution_html:
• Dalit-Bahujan political thought challenges caste oppression- Brahmanical dominance
  • untouchability- social exclusion- advocates equality, dignity, representation, social justice, and
  • redistribution of power- drawing on thinkers such as Phule, Ambedkar, and Periyar, it promotes
  • education, constitutional rights, collective mobilisation, and the emancipation of oppressed
  • communities.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe Kautilya’s views on administration.
questions.solution_html:
• Kautilya- Arthashastra-advocates an efficient, disciplined, and centralised administrative
  • system under a responsible monarch- emphasised ministerial selection- bureaucratic
  • accountability- taxation- espionage- justice and economic management- ruler’s welfare
  • depends upon public welfare- effective administration ensures security, prosperity, stability and
  • political order.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe Abul Fazl’s views on religious tolerance.
questions.solution_html:
• Abul Fazl-Akbar’s court historian and adviser- advocated Sulh-i-Kul- meaning universal
  • peace- he supported religious tolerance, rational inquiry and inclusive governance- irrespective
  • of religious differences- his political philosophy encouraged dialogue among faiths- challenged
  • sectarian prejudice- helped to develop an imperial vision of coexistence and political unity.
questions.final_answer: sectarian prejudice- helped to develop an imperial vision of coexistence and political unity
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Examine Periyar’s opposition to social discrimination.
questions.solution_html:
• E. V. Ramasamy Periyar- challenged caste hierarchy, untouchability, Brahmanical
  • domination and gender inequality- Self-Respect Movement- promoted rationalism, self
  • respect, inter-caste marriage, women’s rights, and equal access to education- radical social
  • philosophy sought to dismantle oppressive traditions and establish dignity, equality, and social
  • justice.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Examine Gandhi’s stance on caste, women, and social reform.
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi opposed untouchability and campaigned for the dignity of oppressed communities
  • although his historical defence of varna differed significantly from Ambedkar’s rejection of
  • caste- he encouraged women’s participation in public life- advocated non-violence- promoted
  • village reconstruction- communal harmony- constructive social reform.
questions.final_answer: village reconstruction- communal harmony- constructive social reform
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe Nehru’s approach towards religious diversity in India.
questions.solution_html:
• Jawaharlal Nehru advocated secularism, religious freedom, and equal citizenship in a
  • pluralistic India- opposed communalism and religious discrimination- emphasised scientific
  • temper, rational inquiry, and democratic institutions- his vision sought national integration
  • through constitutional equality, cultural diversity, modern education- a state independent of
  • religious domination.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Examine the relationship between the Sultan, Shariat and political authority in Barani’s thought.
questions.solution_html:
• Barani viewed the Sultan as the guardian of Islamic law and political order- although
  • Shariat provided moral and religious legitimacy- he recognised the practical necessity of royal
  • regulations (Zawabit) for effective governance- his political thought combined religious
  • orthodoxy- hierarchical social organisation- state authority- subordinated political decisions to
  • Islamic principles while accommodating administrative necessities.
questions.final_answer: Islamic principles while accommodating administrative necessities
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Examine Ram Mohan Roy's engagement with western liberal and Enlightenment political ideas and critically assess his contribution to early Indian constitutional and civil liberties' discourse.
questions.solution_html:
• Ram Mohan Roy embraced Western liberalism- Enlightenment rationalism- individual
  • liberty- constitutional government- critically engaged with Indian traditions- he advocated
  • freedom of the press- judicial reform- religious toleration- civil rights- his petitions and public
  • interventions helped shape early constitutional discourse- Roy’s reformist politics remained
  • largely elite-led and did not establish universal democratic participation.
questions.final_answer: largely elite-led and did not establish universal democratic participation
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Evaluate the significance of Tilak’s political leadership during the rise of extremist nationalism in the early twentieth century.
questions.solution_html:
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak-extremist phase- transformed Indian nationalism through assertive
  • political mobilisation and resistance to British rule- his declaration that Swaraj was a birthright
  • popularised self-government- Swadeshi movement and public festivals encouraged mass
  • participation- his methods challenged moderate constitutional politics- Tilak’s nationalism also
  • contained social conservatism and sometimes relied on religious-cultural symbols.
questions.final_answer: contained social conservatism and sometimes relied on religious-cultural symbols
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Sri Narayana Guru combined spiritual wisdom with practical social reform. / Discuss how his teachings connect inner spiritual growth with outer social change.
questions.solution_html:
• Sri Narayana Guru connected spiritual realisation with social equality-challenged caste
  • discrimination through ethical and religious reform- his principle, “One caste, one religion, one
  • God for humankind”- emphasised shared human dignity-social action through education
  • temple consecrations- institutional initiatives- encouraged oppressed communities’
  • empowerment- demonstrated that inner transformation must support external social justice and
  • collective progress.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
